ranking.note: Raised to P1: LevelDB's exclusive lock is the single limitation blocking the category's headline use case (external tools reading chainstate while a node runs); every other PR here is incremental by comparison.
Placed ahead of #30342 because it defines the connection/context API that #30342 builds on; reviewing it second avoids breaking churn for downstream users.

Lowered to P4: removing two redundant accessors is exactly the cosmetic API polish with no consumer asking for it that the category pins below the misuse-preventing cleanups (#34775, #36353) kept at P3.

inconsistencies: Three PRs rework kernel error propagation and overlap: #29700 (return fatal errors up the stack), #35646 (remove M_ERROR from ValidationState via util::Expected), #36326 (typed FatalError/FlushError across the boundary). #29700 is the foundational one and should be reviewed/decided first; #35646 is an RFC on the same seam and #36326 layers typed representations on top. Deciding them independently risks three incompatible error models in the C API.

#34775 (allow only one global logging connection, because the logger is a process-wide singleton) is in direct conflict with #33847 and #30342 (attach connections per context, per-connection levels, route each context's log to its own connection). These cannot both land as designed; the logging-architecture decision should be taken before either side is reviewed in detail.

Chain order matters: #33847 must precede #30342 (per the description, #30342 depends on it, plus #34778/#34374/#29256), and #30342 in turn unblocks #30343. Reviewing #30342 first wastes effort on an API shape still under discussion.

#36353 only documents that btck_Block caches fChecked so revalidation under different consensus parameters silently passes. That is a real correctness footgun at the API boundary; a reviewer should decide whether a code fix is wanted instead of (or alongside) the header warning.

#35662 touches the same experimental kernel C verification path as #35187 (both deal with txdata/spent-coins supplied by callers); the unintended-copy fix should be checked against #35187's new entry point so the fix is not re-introduced there.
result.notes: Only one P1: the LevelDB reader-lock removal is the one problem whose persistence materially blocks external consumers of the library. The large P2 block is genuinely flat in consequence — API capability additions (#35187, #35557, #35641), the error-propagation seam (#29700, #35646, #36326), the logging seam (#33847, #30342) and the build decoupling (#28690) are all durable-but-deferrable kernel decoupling work; within it I ordered by certainty of benefit to external consumers.
